scores.evidence: The one diagram (Fig. 1, explore → plan → read plan → approve → implement → commit) is a vertical flowchart with Japanese labels that match the body text: 探索/計画 プランモード, 計画を読む, 直したい点がある, 承認, 実装して確かめる, コミット. It has under 12 nodes, the caption states the takeaway (計画を読み、直してから承認して実装に進む), and it stays readable at 390 px (pages/mobile-jp-07.png, pages/mobile-jp-08.png, pages/desktop-jp-05.png). No images, so none are decorative or broken.

textOnlyScreens is empty on both desktop and mobile. Every screen holds a heading, a term table, a figure, a prompt, a code block, steps or a check, and paragraphs stay at 2–4 lines on mobile. Desktop chars per line: median 39, inside the 30–40 target (max 46 on a few lines).

This is a Japanese-only lesson, and it is complete in JP: diagram labels, step titles, prompt placeholders (ログイン画面のファイル, 作りたい機能) and checklists are all in Japanese, and katakana terms carry their English form (ステータスバー（status bar）, エディタ（editor）). The link text 'autoモードが使えない環境' is descriptive, and contrast is adequate on every screen, including the dark code blocks.

niceToHave: reader: the flashcard hint 'クリックまたはスペースキーでめくる' also shows at the 390 px touch viewport (pages/mobile-jp-33.png); a touch wording such as 'タップでめくる' would fit mobile better.

reader: on mobile, todo.html lines 9–12 and 14–15 soft-wrap with a hanging indent (pages/mobile-jp-20.png). The line numbers keep each line readable and the highlighted addItem range (13–18) is still clear, so this is not a lesson defect.
reader: the full-length mobile-jp.png stops at 16000 px (pageHeight 24711); the 35 per-screen PNGs cover the whole lesson.
reader: 13 failed /api/v2/user/* requests (500) are preview-environment noise and are not counted as console errors.

Fig. 1 takes about 1.5 mobile screens (pages/mobile-jp-07.png to pages/mobile-jp-08.png), so the learner scrolls once to see the commit end. This is acceptable, but a shorter label such as '探索（プラン）' would tighten it.
summary: metrics.json shows no hard failures: overflowX false, 0 console, mermaid, unknown-block or broken-image errors, and no text-only screens. All 35 mobile and 23 desktop screens are clean, with no clipped or overlapping text, no controls hidden under the bars and no personal data. The strongest part is the rhythm: term tables, the vertical diagram, prompts, steps and checks alternate so no screen is a wall of text. There are no lesson must-fixes; the remaining notes are reader-level (touch wording on flashcards, code-line wrapping on mobile).
